Research Domains: Developmental and social psychology (nostalgia trajectories in emerging adulthood)
Authenticity and well-being in natural/social contexts

Mediation and serial mediation analyses; experimental-causal-chain framework

Platforms: OSF, GitHub repositories (e.g., FAVEE-HPP; PsychWordVec), pre-trained language models
Application Areas: Naming practices and cultural trend analysis
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Convergent-methods approach: combining longitudinal, cross-cultural, experimental, and computational methods to triangulate findings
Focus on mechanism over correlation: emphasis on mediators and causal-chain frameworks to explain observed associations
Measurement invariance and cross-temporal validation to ensure comparability of constructs across time
Scalability and generalizability: testing universal structures across regions and historical contexts
Specificity of mechanisms: parsing macro-level values and micro-level traits for targeted explanations
Methodological transparency and openness via OSF and code sharing
Summary Description: Dr. Huajian Cai specializes in cross-cultural psychology and computational methods in psychology, with a strong emphasis on how culture and life-events shape core psychological constructs, as well as the development and testing of robust, generalizable models across time and space. His work spans nostalgia trajectories in emerging adulthood, universal representations of human relationships across cultures and history, mechanisms linking nature exposure to authenticity and well-being, and culturally specific changes in naming practices. Cai applies sophisticated longitudinal modeling (TSO; LMA), measurement invariance, time-series and Granger causality analyses, as well as modern embedding-based methods (word embeddings, RSA, WEAT/CEAT) to study cognition, social behavior, and cultural change. He also contributes to methodological tool development (e.g., PsychWordVec in R) and advocates open science via OSF repositories.
